correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs all quantifiers and boundary cases. The first iterate is a positive scalar multiple of the nonnegative right-hand side in every dimension. In dimensions one and two, exact finite termination plus the explicit nonnegative Stieltjes inverse excludes sign loss. The three-dimensional irreducible witness is checked exactly: Sylvester minors 2, 4, and 46 are positive; the inverse is strictly positive; and the second CG iterate equals \( (9076,9469,-32)^{\mathsf T}/3219 \). No finite experiment is used to prove the universal statement.

originality.rationale: The inspected classical CG literature establishes finite termination and norm/Krylov optimality, while M-matrix literature establishes inverse positivity and constrained-CG literature enforces feasibility by changing the method. Focused searches did not locate the sharp statement that classical CG is protected through dimension two but can leave the nonnegative cone at its second iterate in dimension three.
residual_risks: Older iterative-method literature may contain an equivalent componentwise observation under terminology such as monotone iteration, order preservation, or cone invariance that was not recovered.
Several archival CG sources were available only through indexed text or abstract-level access, so absence of the claim from those sources is not asserted beyond the material actually read.

value.rationale: The nonnegative cone is structurally important for inverse-positive discretizations, while CG is selected for its energy/Krylov optimality. The result pinpoints the first place these structures diverge, gives a complete minimal-dimension/minimal-iteration boundary, and supplies a small exact irreducible test case. This is a motivated boundary fact rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
